paragraphs: Indians abroad send home $135 billion a year. Your friend sends photos.

Remitly. Western Union. Every bank. They all fight for that money every single month, and none of them care about the friend.
Most of them say "zero fee" and earn on the exchange rate instead. Wise is the rare one that shows its fee upfront.
And slowly, you stop being part of each other's day. No random calls. Just "we should catch up", moved to next weekend. Again.
Your good news reaches them while they sleep. Their bad news reaches you a day late. The friendship now runs on a delay.
Then they come home for three weeks. Family gets every evening. You get one dinner, and you'll take it.
No one is wrong here. They went where the salary was, and you stayed where the family is. It still hurts.
**The money comes home every month. Your friend comes home once a year.**

cover.headline: Your best friend didn't leave when they moved abroad.
cover.sub: The friendship just got visiting hours.

paragraphs: Your best friend didn't leave when they moved abroad.
The friendship just got visiting hours.
The first year, nothing changes. Video calls on Sunday, voice notes at 2 AM their time, "bas yaar, tu bata."
Then the time zone starts winning.
Your good news reaches them while they're asleep. Their bad news reaches you a day late, already handled.
You stop being in each other's day. You become each other's update.
Indians abroad send home about $135 billion a year, and every bank and app fights for that money every month.
What the friendships pay never shows up anywhere.
They pay in calls moved to "next weekend." In birthdays wished a day late. In a wedding watched on a livestream, sound off, in a meeting.
Then December comes, and they're home for three weeks. Parents get the mornings. Relatives get the evenings. In-laws get a weekend.
You get one dinner, and you take it.
At that dinner you notice it. The jokes still land, but you're talking about the past, not the plan.
The friendship isn't gone. It stopped growing.
Nobody did anything wrong. They went where the salary was. You stayed where the parents are.
Both of you call it the right decision, and both of you are right.
The friendships that survive a time zone aren't the ones with the longest calls.
They're the ones where someone calls on a random Tuesday with nothing to say.
The money comes home every month.
Your friend comes home once a year.
